description: Schema version used to decode and migrate the row
notes: Start at 1 and increment only for incompatible evolution

description: Stable SwiftData/Core Data account UUID
notes: Part of both the mailbox-location key and provider correlation keys

description: Stable SwiftData/Core Data mailbox UUID
notes: The mailbox-location key is account_id, mailbox_id, uid_validity, and uid

description: IMAP mailbox name captured when the row is written
notes: Useful when files are inspected without the model store

description: IMAP UIDVALIDITY for the containing mailbox
notes: Part of the durable message identity

description: Mailbox-local stable IMAP UID
notes: Sequence number is intentionally excluded because it is transient

description: Calendar partition formatted as YYYY-MM
notes: Convert the first usable value to UTC: internal_date, then an unambiguous sent_at, then metadata_fetched_at; never infer a timezone for an ambiguous Date header

description: When this metadata was most recently fetched from IMAP
notes: Store UTC

description: When the message was first observed by SeleneTide
notes: Store UTC and preserve across refreshes

description: When this Parquet row was most recently changed
notes: Store UTC

description: Normalized system flags and provider or user keywords
notes: Use an empty list rather than null

description: Server delivery or storage timestamp normalized to UTC
notes: Retain the original offset separately; null only when the server value is unavailable or invalid

description: Original INTERNALDATE offset from UTC in minutes
notes: Supports display and forensic analysis

description: Approximate encoded RFC message size in bytes
notes: May include headers body and encoded attachments

description: Sender-supplied Date header normalized to UTC
notes: Null when missing, invalid, or timezone-ambiguous; never assume the device timezone

description: Original Date-header offset from UTC in minutes
notes: Preserves the sender timezone offset

description: Decoded message subject
notes: Decode RFC 2047 encoded words

description: Normalized author addresses
notes: Use an empty list when malformed or unavailable

description: Agent that sent the message when distinct from From
notes: Often absent

description: Normalized reply destination addresses
notes: Use an empty list when absent

description: Normalized primary recipient addresses
notes: Does not expose hidden SMTP envelope recipients

description: Normalized carbon-copy recipient addresses
notes: Use an empty list when absent

description: Normalized Bcc addresses retained in the stored message
notes: Usually empty because delivery commonly removes this header

description: Canonical bracketed sender-generated message identifier
notes: Not guaranteed present or globally unique

description: Referenced parent Message-ID values
notes: Use an empty list for root messages

description: Ordered ancestor Message-ID values
notes: Preserve header order

description: Original server BODYSTRUCTURE representation
notes: Optional diagnostic source for parser evolution

parquet_type: LIST<STRUCT<part_id: STRING, parent_part_id: STRING, media_type: STRING, media_subtype: STRING, parameters: MAP<STRING, STRING>, disposition: STRING, filename: STRING, content_id: STRING, content_languages: LIST<STRING>, transfer_encoding: STRING, encoded_size_bytes: INT64, is_multipart: BOOLEAN, is_attachment: BOOLEAN, is_inline: BOOLEAN>>
description: Normalized MIME tree nodes
notes: Parent identifiers preserve hierarchy; contains attachment metadata without content bytes

description: Number of MIME leaf parts
notes: Derived from mime_parts

description: Normalized top-level media type such as multipart/mixed
notes: Exclude parameters from this value

description: Normalized top-level content-type parameters
notes: May include a boundary value; use an empty map when absent

description: Normalized top-level disposition
notes: Part-level dispositions live in mime_parts

description: Normalized BCP 47 language tags
notes: Use an empty list when absent

description: Recorded envelope-return or bounce address
notes: Semantics depend on the receiving system

description: Provider-recorded delivery aliases or mailbox addresses
notes: Provider-dependent and potentially repeated

description: Raw Received headers in message order
notes: Earlier hops are untrusted and may be forged

parquet_type: LIST<STRUCT<from_host: STRING, by_host: STRING, protocol: STRING, message_id: STRING, for_address: STRING, received_at: TIMESTAMP(MICROS, true), raw_value: STRING>>
description: Best-effort parsed delivery hops in message order
notes: Keep raw_value because Received syntax and trust vary

parquet_type: LIST<STRUCT<authserv_id: STRING, method: STRING, result: STRING, properties: MAP<STRING, STRING>, raw_value: STRING>>
description: Parsed email-authentication outcomes plus their raw values
notes: Trust policy must identify the authoritative receiving server

description: Parsed SPF result and original field value
notes: Provider-dependent fallback when Authentication-Results is absent

parquet_type: LIST<STRUCT<domain: STRING, selector: STRING, algorithm: STRING, identity: STRING, raw_value: STRING>>
description: DKIM signing domains selectors algorithms identities and raw values
notes: Signature presence does not prove successful validation

description: Mailing-list display name and identifier
notes: Strong list signal when present

description: Ordered mailto and HTTPS unsubscribe URIs
notes: Use an empty list when absent

description: Whether RFC-style one-click unsubscribe is declared
notes: False when absent

description: URIs used to submit mail to a list
notes: Use an empty list when absent

description: Normalized auto-submission token
notes: Examples include no auto-generated and auto-replied

description: Normalized legacy precedence token
notes: Non-standard and insufficient alone for classification

description: Decoded sending-software identifier
notes: Untrusted and often absent

description: Decoded composing or sending client identifier
notes: Untrusted and often absent

description: Normalized importance value
notes: Prefer high normal or low when recognizable

description: Normalized declared priority value
notes: Different clients use different vocabularies

description: Parsed legacy numeric priority
notes: Normally 1 through 5 when parseable

description: Decoded sender-declared organization
notes: Non-standard sparse and untrusted

description: Gmail account-wide message correlation identifier
notes: Store as decimal text; account_id plus gmail_message_id correlates label copies but does not replace the mailbox-location key

description: Gmail native thread identifier
notes: Store as decimal text for lossless cross-tool compatibility

description: Decoded Gmail labels
notes: Use an empty list for non-Gmail accounts

description: Lowercased domain from normalized From or Sender address
notes: Document which address wins when several exist

description: Sorted unique lowercased domains from visible normalized recipient addresses
notes: Use an empty list when no valid recipient domain is available

description: Hour of day from sent_at using the original sender offset
notes: Range 0 through 23; null when Date or its offset is unavailable

description: ISO weekday from sent_at using the original sender offset
notes: Range 1 Monday through 7 Sunday

description: Hour of day from internal_date normalized to UTC
notes: Range 0 through 23; null when internal_date is unavailable

description: ISO weekday from internal_date normalized to UTC
notes: Range 1 Monday through 7 Sunday; null when internal_date is unavailable

description: Message relationship to the account: inbound outbound self or unknown
notes: Compare normalized addresses with the primary account address and observed Delivered-To aliases

description: Count of unique normalized visible To Cc and retained Bcc addresses
notes: Does not include hidden SMTP recipients

description: Count of unique normalized To addresses
notes: Useful for direct-versus-broadcast analysis

description: Count of unique normalized Cc addresses
notes: Use zero when Cc is absent

description: Count of MIME parts classified as attachments
notes: Use a stable documented classification rule

description: Whether attachment_count is greater than zero
notes: Convenient for grouping and CSV exports

description: Sum of encoded_size_bytes for parts classified as attachments
notes: Use zero when none exist and null when any attachment size is unknown

description: Primary body shape: plain html alternative mixed or other
notes: Use a versioned deterministic MIME classification rule

description: Unicode character count of the decoded subject
notes: Null when Subject is absent and zero when it is present but empty

description: Approximate depth derived from ordered References
notes: Malformed or absent References reduce accuracy

description: internal_date minus sent_at in milliseconds
notes: May be negative because sender clocks can be wrong

description: Whether FLAGS contains Seen
notes: Does not prove that a human read the message

description: Whether FLAGS contains Answered
notes: Provider and client behavior may be imperfect

description: Whether FLAGS contains Flagged
notes: Useful for measuring user-marked importance

description: Documented classification from list and automation headers
notes: Use a versioned deterministic classifier

description: Version of the bulk-classification rule
notes: Required whenever bulk_classification is populated
